mainTopic: Betrothing with payment for work, and betrothal where the item or claim turns out different (רבי שמעון: הטעה לשבח)
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about a craftsman who betroths a woman with payment for his work. It gives three explanations: when a wage becomes owed, whether an אומן owns the שבח כלי, and a case of מלוה ופרוטה where he added a jewel of his own. It then shows the same arguments in a ברייתא between the תנא קמא, רבי נתן, and רבי יהודה הנשיא. Next, a new משנה rules that if a man betroths with something that turns out different from what he said, she is not betrothed. רבי שמעון says that if the change is to her advantage, she is betrothed. The גמרא settles three ברייתות about 'this cup' by saying each is about a different liquid. It then challenges רבי שמעון, since some people may prefer silver to gold. After אביי's answer is rejected, רבא explains the case as a woman's שליח who was given a gold coin wrapped in a cloth. Finally, אביי says three תנאים share the view of מראה מקום הוא לו, and the proof from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First explanation: when is the wage owed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its first explanation of the dispute. One side (רבי מאיר) holds that a wage is owed only at the end of the job. The other side (חכמים) holds that it builds up from the beginning to the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One Sage holds:] the wage is owed only at the end. And the other Sage holds: the wage builds up from the beginning until the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why רבי מאיר and חכמים argue. They disagree about when a worker's wage becomes owed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that betrothing with a מלוה (an existing debt) does not work. According to רבי מאיר, the wage only becomes owed at the very end, so it never turns into a debt and can serve as קידושין money. According to חכמים, the wage has been piling up the whole time, so by the end it is already a debt, and she is not betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: Hired work; the obligation to pay a wage
From the beginning until the end, building up continuously

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the argument here is about whether a loan can be used for קידושין. Both sides agree it cannot. The only question is whether this wage ever counted as a loan.

phrases.english: the wage is owed only at the end.
And the other Sage holds:
the wage is owed continuously, from the beginning until the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first explanation of the dispute, which began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Locating the dispute in a different underlying principle (when wages become owed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about whether a loan works for קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree a loan does not work. They argue about whether the wage became a loan at all.

steps.title: Second explanation: does a craftsman own the improvement?
steps.stepSummary: Here everyone agrees that wages build up from the beginning, and that betrothing with a loan does not work. Instead, the argument is about whether an אומן (craftsman) acquires the שבח כלי, the added value he put into the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: everyone agrees the wage builds up from beginning to end, and one who betroths with a loan, she is not betrothed. Here they argue about whether a craftsman acquires the improvement of the vessel. One Sage holds he does; the other holds he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different way to explain the dispute. It moves the argument to the question of whether a craftsman owns the value he added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the אומן owns the improvement (רבי מאיר), then when he hands her the jewelry he is giving her something of his own, and that works as קידושין. If he does not own it (חכמים), he is only collecting a wage. That wage is a debt she owes him, which cannot be used for קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible explanation
Betrothing with a loan, an existing debt
The added value or improvement of an item

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of אומן קונה בשבח כלי is a well-known principle that appears in many places in ש״ס, especially in the laws of workers and damages.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
that everyone agrees the wage is owed
continuously from the beginning until the end,
and one who betroths with a loan, she is not betrothed,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא, בְּאוּמָּן קוֹנָה בִּשְׁבַח כְּלִי קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and here, they disagree about whether a craftsman acquires the improvement of the vessel.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: אוּמָּן קוֹנָה בִּשְׁבַח כְּלִי,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: a craftsman acquires the improvement of the vessel,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר: אֵין אוּמָּן קוֹנֶה בִּשְׁבַח כְּלִי.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: a craftsman does not acquire the improvement of the vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יֶשְׁנָהּ לִשְׂכִירוּת מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first explanation. Everyone now agrees with the חכמים' view on wages, and the dispute moves to a new principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative explanation of what the dispute is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute is about when wages become owed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It could instead be about whether an אומן owns the שבח כלי.

steps.title: Third explanation: he added a jewel of his own
steps.stepSummary: Here everyone agrees on both earlier points. The case is one where the craftsman added a small jewel of his own. The argument is whether, when a man gives a loan plus a פרוטה, his mind is on the פרוטה (רבי מאיר) or on the loan (חכמים).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: everyone agrees a craftsman does not acquire the improvement, that wages build up from start to end, and that betrothing with a loan does not work. Here we are dealing with a case where he added a jewel of his own. One Sage holds that with a loan and a פרוטה, his mind is on the פרוטה; the other holds his mind is on the loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third explanation. It keeps every earlier principle agreed upon and sets up a specific case: he added his own jewel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added jewel is something new that he gives her, worth at least a פרוטה, alongside the wage debt. If the giver is focused on the פרוטה (רבי מאיר), the jewel makes the קידושין work. If he is focused on the loan (חכמים), the קידושין are based on the debt, so they fail.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? Introduces a specific case setting
A loan plus a פרוטה, given together for קידושין

steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of רבי מאיר versus חכמים: (1) when wages become owed, (2) אומן קונה בשבח כלי, and (3) מלוה ופרוטה, where he added his own jewel.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין אוּמָּן קוֹנָה בִּשְׁבַח כְּלִי,
phrases.english: that everyone agrees a craftsman does not acquire the improvement of the vessel,
and the wage is owed continuously from the beginning until the end,
and one who betroths with a loan, she is not betrothed,
and with what case are we dealing here?
For example, where he added a jewel of his own for her.
For one Sage holds: with a loan and a פרוטה,
his mind is on the פרוטה,
and the other Sage holds: his mind is on the loan.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין אוּמָּן קוֹנָה בִּשְׁבַח כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation that accepts the agreed principles of both earlier explanations and moves the dispute to a narrower case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the case (אוקימתא) so the dispute is about a different principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute must be about wages or about אומן קונה בשבח כלי.
steps.terutzMaskana: It may be about a case of מלוה ופרוטה, where he added his own jewel.

steps.title: The same dispute appears among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this dispute matches an argument between תנאים in a ברייתא. The תנא קמא rules that 'for the work I already did' does not create קידושין, but 'for the work I will do' does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they argue along the lines of a dispute between these תנאים, as it is taught: 'With the wage for what I have worked for you,' she is not betrothed. 'With the wage for what I will work for you,' she is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the same kind of argument already existed among the תנאים. This step quotes the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Payment for work already done is a debt, so it cannot be used for קידושין. Payment for future work works for the תנא קמא, because he holds the wage only becomes owed at the end. At that moment it is as if he gives her the money for קידושין. This matches the first explanation, where רבי מאיר holds the wage is owed only at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the sages of the משנה era
As it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And they disagree along the lines of the dispute between these תנאים,
as it is taught:
'With the payment for what I have worked for you,' she is not betrothed.
'With the payment for what I will work for you,' she is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds the explanations just given in a ברייתא. Step 7 shows it holds both the wage dispute (Step 1) and the מלוה ופרוטה dispute (Step 3).
steps.raayaObject: The explanations of the dispute between רבי מאיר and חכמים: when a wage is owed, and where the mind is with מלוה ופרוטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא קידושין 3:4) with a dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי נתן.

steps.title: רבי נתן: even future work does not create קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן disagrees with the תנא קמא. He holds that even 'for the work I will do' does not create קידושין, and certainly 'for the work I already did' does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: 'With the payment for what I will work for you,' she is not betrothed, and all the more so 'With the payment for what I have worked for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי נתן's opposing view. This completes the picture of the dispute between the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן holds that the wage builds up from the beginning to the end. So by the time the work is done, the payment is already a debt, and a debt cannot be used for קידושין. His view matches the חכמים in the first explanation, while the תנא קמא matches רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא equals רבי מאיר: the wage is owed only at the end, so future work works for קידושין. רבי נתן equals חכמים: the wage builds up all along and becomes a debt, so neither past nor future work works.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
'With the payment for what I will work for you,' she is not betrothed,
and all the more so 'With the payment for what I have worked for you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the ברייתא, giving the opposing opinion to the תנא קמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment for work, whether past or future, cannot create קידושין, because by the end it is a debt.

steps.title: The third opinion: neither wage works unless he adds a jewel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנשיא rules that both 'for the work I already did' and 'for the work I will do' fail to create קידושין. If the craftsman adds a small jewel of his own, she is betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה הנשיא says: In truth they said that whether he says 'with the wage for the work I did' or 'with the wage for the work I will do for you,' she is not betrothed. But if he added a small jewel of his own, she is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third opinion, after the תנא קמא and רבי נתן. רבי יהודה הנשיא agrees that the wage alone does not work, but a jewel added from the craftsman's own property does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the wage itself, רבי יהודה הנשיא sounds just like רבי נתן: neither past nor future work creates קידושין. What he adds is the jewel case. A jewel added on top of the wage makes the קידושין work, which recalls the case from Step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי, the editor of the משנה, giving a third opinion here
'In truth they said,' a phrase that introduces a firm, settled rule

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:
In truth they said:
whether he says 'with the wage for the work I did,'
or 'with the wage for the work I will do for you,'
she is not betrothed.
And if he added for her a small jewel of his own,
she is betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא אוֹמֵר: בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the third opinion in the same ברייתא, after the תנא קמא (Step 4) and רבי נתן (Step 5).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wage for past or future work does not create קידושין. A jewel the craftsman adds of his own does.

steps.title: Mapping how the three opinions in the ברייתא differ
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא and רבי נתן argue about how a wage is owed. רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא argue about a loan plus a פרוטה: is the man's mind on the loan or on the פרוטה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Between the תנא קמא and רבי נתן, the difference is about wages. Between רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא, the difference is about a loan plus a פרוטה. One master (רבי נתן) holds that with a loan plus a פרוטה, his mind is on the loan. The other master (רבי יהודה הנשיא) holds that his mind is on the פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly where each pair of opinions in the ברייתא disagrees. It ties them back to the explanations given earlier in Steps 1 and 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first argument, between the תנא קמא and רבי נתן, is the wage question from Step 1. The second argument, between רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא, is the loan-plus-פרוטה question from Step 3. רבי נתן says the jewel does not help, because the man is thinking about the loan. רבי יהודה הנשיא says it does help, because he is thinking about the פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
'There is between them,' meaning the practical difference between two opinions
Wages, and how the debt for them builds up
A loan together with one פרוטה of real value
His mind, meaning what he is really focused on

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא matches the two earlier explanations of the dispute. תנא קמא against רבי נתן is about wages. רבי נתן against רבי יהודה הנשיא is about whether the mind is on the loan or on the פרוטה.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'מר' is רבי נתן (mind on the loan, so the jewel does not help). The second 'מר' is רבי יהודה הנשיא (mind on the פרוטה, so she is betrothed).

phrases.english: Between the first Tanna and Rabbi Natan
the difference between them is wages,
phrases.notes: This is the question from Step 1: is a wage owed bit by bit from the start, or only at the end?

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין רַבִּי נָתָן לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא –
phrases.english: between Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
the difference between them is a loan plus a peruta.
One master holds: with a loan plus a peruta,
his mind is on the loan,
and the other master holds: his mind is on the peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין תַּנָּא קַמָּא לְרַבִּי נָתָן אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ שְׂכִירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the three opinions just quoted (Steps 4 through 6) and ties them to the earlier explanations.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא contains both earlier disputes. One is about how wages are owed, and the other is about where the mind is with a loan plus a פרוטה.

steps.title: New משנה: betrothal with a gift or a claim that turns out different
steps.stepSummary: Sometimes the item a man betroths with, or his own description of himself, turns out different from what he said. The חכמים say she is not betrothed. רבי שמעון says that if the change is to her advantage, she is betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man says: 'Be betrothed to me with this cup of wine,' and it turns out to be honey. Or he says honey, and it turns out to be wine. Or 'with this silver דינר,' and it turns out to be gold. Or gold, and it turns out to be silver. Or 'on condition that I am rich,' and he turns out to be poor. Or 'poor,' and he turns out to be rich. In all these cases she is not betrothed. רבי שמעון says: if he misled her in a way that is better for her, she is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists cases where what the man said does not match reality, and gives the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair goes both ways: worse than he said, and better than he said. The first opinion rules that any mismatch cancels the קידושין, even one in her favor. רבי שמעון disagrees only when the mistake is to her advantage, because then she surely would have agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin, which can be silver or gold
He misled her in a way that benefits her

steps.confusionAlert: The first opinion says she is not betrothed even when the mistake helps her, like gold instead of silver. Only רבי שמעון makes a difference for a change in her favor.

phrases.english: MISHNA: 'Be betrothed to me with this cup of wine,'
and it turned out to be honey;
'of honey,' and it turned out to be wine;

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּדִינָר זֶה שֶׁל כֶּסֶף״ וְנִמְצָא שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: 'with this silver dinar,' and it turned out to be gold;
'of gold,' and it turned out to be silver;
'on condition that I am rich,' and he turned out to be poor;
'poor,' and he turned out to be rich;
she is not betrothed.
Rabbi Shimon says:
If he misled her to her advantage, she is betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לִי בְּכוֹס זֶה שֶׁל יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It starts a new topic, unconnected to the wage discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion: any mismatch between what he said and reality cancels the קידושין. רבי שמעון: a mismatch in her favor does not cancel it.

steps.title: Three ברייתות disagree about 'this cup'
steps.stepSummary: A man says 'be betrothed with this cup.' Three ברייתות give three different answers: the cup and its contents, the cup only, or the contents only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: when a man says 'Be betrothed to me with this cup,' one ברייתא teaches she is betrothed with the cup and what is inside it. Another teaches with the cup but not what is inside it. Another teaches with what is inside it but not the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings three ברייתות on the משנה's 'this cup' case, and they seem to contradict each other. This sets up the next step, which will resolve them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what exactly the קידושין money is when a man hands over a full cup. All three possible answers appear in different ברייתות. That is a clear contradiction the גמרא must settle.

keyTerms.meaning: With what is inside it, meaning the contents

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
'Be betrothed to me with this cup,'
one teaches: with it and with what is inside it;

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: בּוֹ וְלֹא בַּמֶּה שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ.
phrases.english: and another teaches: with it but not with what is inside it.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: בַּמֶּה שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ וְלֹא בּוֹ.
phrases.english: And another teaches: with what is inside it but not with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לִי בְּכוֹס זֶה, תָּנֵי חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה's cup case by bringing ברייתות that seem to contradict each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three sources give three different answers for the very same words, so they cannot all be right as they stand.

steps.title: Each ברייתא is about a different liquid
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. Each ברייתא is talking about a cup filled with something different: water, wine, or oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is not difficult: this ברייתא is about water, this one is about wine, and this one is about oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction from the last step. Each ברייתא is speaking about a different liquid in the cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on what is inside the cup. With cheap water, he is really giving the cup. With wine, רש״י explains, he is really giving the wine, since people drink it and hand the cup back. With ציהרא, a fish brine (or oil) that is kept in its cup for a long time, he is giving both the cup and what's in it. So the three ברייתות describe three different situations and do not actually disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is not difficult,' introducing a resolution

steps.whatToRemember: With 'this cup,' what she is betrothed with depends on what the cup holds. This is how the גמרא settles three ברייתות that seemed to clash.

phrases.english: And it is not difficult:
this one is about water,
phrases.notes: These don't follow the listed order. Water is worth little, so it fits 'the cup, not what's inside'; wine fits 'both,' and oil fits 'what's inside, not the cup.'

phrases.english: this one is about wine,
this one is about oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the contradiction between the three ברייתות in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases: each source is about a different liquid in the cup
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to argue about the very same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא is about a cup holding a different liquid (water, wine, or oil), so they do not conflict.

steps.title: Isn't 'better' a matter of personal taste?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's rule from the משנה and challenges it. A משנה about wine and vinegar shows that some people prefer one and some prefer the other. So maybe some people prefer silver over gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he misled her for the better, she is betrothed. But doesn't רבי שמעון accept this rule: if someone sold wine and it turned out to be vinegar, or vinegar and it turned out to be wine, both sides can back out? This shows that some people prefer vinegar and some prefer wine. Here too, some people prefer silver and do not want gold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's rule from the משנה and attacks it with a rule about selling wine and vinegar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון assumes gold is clearly 'better' than silver, so she should be happy and the קידושין work. But in the wine and vinegar case, the seller who gave wine instead of vinegar can still back out, so wine is not treated as simply 'better.' If 'better' depends on what each person wants, then gold instead of silver might not be better for her either.

keyTerms.meaning: He misled her for the better (the reality was better than what he said)
To back out of the deal
It suits him / he prefers it

steps.confusionAlert: The first line is not a new statement. It is the גמרא quoting רבי שמעון from the משנה (Step 8) so it can question it.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הִטְעָהּ לְשֶׁבַח הֲרֵי זוֹ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: If he misled her for the better, she is betrothed.
But doesn't Rabbi Shimon accept this:
wine, and it turned out to be vinegar,
vinegar, and it turned out to be wine –
both of them can back out.
This shows that some people prefer vinegar
and some people prefer wine.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי: אִיכָּא נִיחָא לֵיהּ בְּכַסְפָּא
phrases.english: Here too: some people prefer silver
and do not want gold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי שמעון's view from Step 8 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule that a change for the better still creates קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wine/vinegar rule shows that 'better' depends on the person, so gold instead of silver may not be better for her.

steps.title: אביי: a man's agent who lent gold instead of silver
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the משנה as a case where a man asked his שליח to lend him a silver דינר and betroth a woman with it, but the שליח lent him gold. The argument is whether the man insisted on silver or only gave a suggestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: I found אביי sitting and explaining it to his son. What case is this? A man told his agent: 'Lend me a silver דינר and go betroth such-and-such a woman for me with it.' The agent went and lent him a gold one. One Sage holds the man was strict about it. The other Sage holds he was only giving a suggestion.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by moving the case to a man's שליח, so the question is not about her taste at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the dispute is about the sender's words, not about whether gold is 'better.' The תנא קמא holds the sender really meant silver, so the שליח did not do what he was told. רבי שמעון holds 'silver' was only a general guide, so the gold still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Being strict; insisting on exactly what was said
Literally 'showing a place'; only giving a suggestion, not a strict condition

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
I found Abaye sitting
and explaining it to his son:
What case are we dealing with here?
For example, where he said to his agent:
'Lend me a silver dinar,
and go betroth such-and-such a woman for me'
and he went and lent him a gold one.
One Sage holds: he was strict about it.
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, who says she is not betrothed.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מַרְאֶה מָקוֹם הוּא לוֹ.
phrases.english: And one Sage holds: he was only giving him a suggestion.
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון. 'Silver' was just a guide, so gold is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) as a man's agent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a woman getting gold instead of silver, which depends on her personal taste.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a man's שליח who lent gold. The dispute is whether the sender's 'silver' was a strict demand or only a suggestion.

steps.title: אביי's case does not fit the משנה's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's answer with three wording problems. The משנה says 'to me' and 'misled her,' and it says the gold was 'found,' but in a שליח case none of these fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'be betrothed to me'? It should say 'be betrothed to him'! Why 'he misled her for the better'? It should say 'he misled him for the better'! And why 'it turned out'? It was gold from the very start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer by showing that three words in the משנה do not match a case of a man's שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a שליח is speaking for the man, he would say 'be betrothed to him,' not 'to me.' The one misled is the sender, not the woman, so it should say 'misled him.' And the שליח knew he was giving gold, so nothing was 'found out' later.

phrases.english: If so, why 'be betrothed to me'?
It should have said 'be betrothed to him'!
Why 'he misled her for the better'?
It should have said 'he misled him for the better'!
phrases.notes: In אביי's case, the שליח 'misled' the man who sent him, not the woman.

phrases.english: And why 'it turned out'?
It was known to be gold from the very start!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי ״הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לִי״? ״הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לוֹ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation that the case is about a man's שליח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'to me,' 'misled her,' and 'found' do not fit a case where a man's שליח knowingly used gold.

steps.title: רבא: the woman's agent got a gold coin wrapped in a cloth
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the case as a woman who sent her שליח to accept קידושין from a man who promised a silver דינר, and the man gave a gold one. The dispute is whether she insisted on silver. 'Found' fits because the coin was wrapped in a cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: I and the 'lion of the group' explained it. Who is that? רבי חייא בר אבין. What case is this? She told her agent: 'Go and accept my קידושין from so-and-so, who told me: Be betrothed to me with a silver דינר.' The man went and gave the agent a gold דינר. One Sage holds she was strict about it. The other Sage holds she was only giving a suggestion. And why does it say 'it turned out'? Because the coin was wrapped in a cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new explanation of the משנה that fits all three wording problems from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man himself said 'be betrothed to me,' and he gave the gold, so he 'misled her.' The agent did not know it was gold because it was wrapped in a cloth, so it was only 'found out' later. The dispute is whether the woman's 'silver' was a strict demand or only a guide.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'lion of the group,' a title of honor for a great scholar
A rag or piece of cloth

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is רבא's: the woman's שליח received a gold coin wrapped in a cloth. The argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון is whether she was strict about silver or only giving a suggestion. So רבי שמעון does not depend on the claim that gold is 'better' for everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the wine/vinegar challenge. רבי שמעון is not saying gold is better for every person. He says her mention of silver was not a strict condition.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
I and the lion of the group
explained it:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the one in square brackets. Both mean 'we explained.'

phrases.english: And who is that? Rabbi Chiya bar Avin.
What case are we dealing with here?
For example, where she said to her agent:
'Go and accept my betrothal for me from so-and-so,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר לִי הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לִי בְּדִינָר שֶׁל כֶּסֶף״
phrases.english: who said to me: Be betrothed to me with a silver dinar'

phrases.aramaic: וְהָלַךְ וְנָתַן לוֹ דִּינָר שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: and the man went and gave him a gold dinar.
One Sage holds: she was strict about it.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מַרְאֶה מָקוֹם הִיא לוֹ,
phrases.english: And one Sage holds: she was only giving him a suggestion.
And what does 'it turned out' mean?
That the coin was wrapped in a cloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new explanation that solves the wording problems of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New redefinition of the case (אוקימתא) as the woman's agent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case was a man's שליח (אביי), which did not fit the משנה's words.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is the woman's שליח who received a gold דינר wrapped in a cloth. The dispute is whether she was strict about silver or only giving a suggestion.

steps.title: Three תנאים share one view: the detail was only a suggestion
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי שמעון, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and רבי אלעזר all hold that a stated detail is only 'מראה מקום', a suggestion and not a demand.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי שמעון, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and רבי אלעזר all hold that when a person names a detail, he is just showing the other person the way. He is not insisting on it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes a general statement. Three different תנאים all hold the same principle: a detail someone names can be just a suggestion, not a strict demand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון's משנה, the question was whether 'silver' was a strict condition or only a suggestion. רבי שמעון said she is מקודשת, so he treats it as a suggestion. אביי now says this is not just רבי שמעון's view. Two other תנאים hold the same idea in other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'he is showing him a place.' The detail is a suggestion of how to do it, not a strict demand.
All of them hold (the same view)
A תנא, the נשיא; his view will be proven from another משנה
A third תנא whom אביי includes in this group

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns one ruling into a shared principle. אביי shows that רבי שמעון's idea, that a named detail can be only a suggestion and not a strict condition, is also held by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
and Rabbi Elazar
all of them hold
he is just showing him a place.
phrases.notes: He means the detail he named was only pointing the way. It was not a strict condition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כּוּלְּהוּ סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's explanation of רבי שמעון's משנה and widens it into a principle shared by three תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and רבי אלעזר all treat a stated detail as מראה מקום, a suggestion rather than a strict condition.

steps.title: Proving the shared view, starting with רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where each תנא holds this view. For רבי שמעון it is the משנה just discussed. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל it begins quoting another משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where does רבי שמעון hold this? In the משנה we just discussed. Where does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל hold this? In a משנה we learned:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts backing up אביי's claim one תנא at a time. The last words set up a quote from a new משנה, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, no new source is needed. His ruling about the silver and gold דינר already shows this view. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the גמרא needs a different משנה, and it starts to bring it with 'דתנן'.

keyTerms.meaning: This that we (just) said, pointing back to the earlier source
As we learned in a משנה. It introduces a quote from a משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon: this that we said,
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי שמעון's משנה about the silver and gold דינר, from the steps just before.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: as we learned in a mishna:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל – דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts proving אביי's claim from step 15, one תנא at a time.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that all three תנאים hold מראה מקום הוא לו
steps.raayaSupportSource: For רבי שמעון: the earlier משנה about the silver and gold דינר. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a משנה about to be quoted.
